analysis: Examined the two head_text units of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (lines 46476-48118). The file is a public synthetic golden-vector fixture for prompt-contract/template/token planning (multi_system, nulls, reasoning_effort, response_text, tool_call_arguments_bridge cases). The patch excerpt shows head changes adding template_input.additional_context {enable_thinking:false} and changing prompt_token_count, chain_hash and token_ids in some vectors. The visible units are data-only: placeholder strings like 'Public followup.' and 'Public synthetic cache-parity input.', repeated token IDs, and hex chain hashes. I saw no secrets, credentials, real consumer prompts, or keys. I found no code paths, authorization logic, attestation handling, encryption, or network behavior changed here. The only security relevance is indirect, through the prefix-cache threat T-041: chain_hash and prompt_contract_id values determine cache-block identity and keying. The visible portion shows a stable prompt_contract_id (507d6d7a...) across the vectors and unchanged block-boundary semantics (256-token blocks). The patch for other vectors (around base 3017-4003 and others) changed the prompt contract ID in places, but I could not see all of those hunks; the excerpt is truncated. Remaining integration question: whether the Swift provider and Go coordinator implementations consuming these vectors (not supplied) derive the same prompt_contract_id, chain hashes and enable_thinking handling, since a parity mismatch could cause cache misses or wrong cache sharing across contracts. That is an unverified contract rather than a supported finding. No regressions identified in the supplied evidence.
